title: Prescriptions Terms for Patients: One Record per Written Order
content:
A patient may hold any number of prescription records under Kestrel Prescriptions; there is no limit on how many records one patient holds.

## The terms

1. Each record is one written order for one drug and strength from one prescriber.
2. Each order is entered as its own record with its own Kestrel prescription number.
3. Two orders are never merged into one record.
4. How records for the same drug and strength interact is decided by the Prescriptions rule on same-drug replacement.

## Applied to hypothetical orders

| Orders presented | Records held |
|---|---|
| One prescriber writes two different drugs | Two records, two Kestrel prescription numbers |
| Two prescribers each write the same drug and strength | Two records, two Kestrel prescription numbers; never merged into one |
| One order for one drug and strength | One record |

**Is there a cap on how many prescriptions one patient can keep at Kestrel?** No. A patient may hold any number of prescription records.
